title: Binary search
summary: Find a value in sorted data by halving the remaining range.

scenario.briefing: A sorted list of product codes is too large to scan one by one. Implement binary search that returns the index of a target or -1.

objectives.description: Find a target index in sorted data.
Reason about why the search range halves.

hints: Keep low and high bounds and compare the middle value.
If the middle is too small, move low above the middle.
If the middle is too large, move high below the middle.
Use while (low <= high), compute mid, compare values, and update low or high.

misconceptions.description: Using strict bounds that skip the remaining single element.
misconceptions.feedback: The loop must include the case low === high. Use while (low <= high).

misconceptions.description: Believing binary search scans every element.
misconceptions.feedback: Each comparison discards half of the remaining range, so the time grows logarithmically.

sections.title: Sorted order enables halving
sections.body: If the data is sorted, comparing the middle value tells you which half cannot contain the target. Binary search discards half the remaining range on each step. Unsorted data cannot support this decision.

sections.title: Complexity describes growth
sections.body: Linear search is O(n): doubling the data roughly doubles the work. Binary search is O(log n). The boundary conditions at the ends of the range are the most common source of bugs.

vocabulary.definition: A search that halves a sorted range each step.
Growing with the logarithm of the input size.
A condition that stays true throughout an algorithm.

steps.title: Implement binary search
steps.prompt: Edit search.js. binarySearch(sorted, target) returns the target index or -1. The input is sorted ascending.

steps.title: Why does it halve?

statements.label: Each comparison can eliminate half the remaining elements.
The low === high case must still be checked.

steps.explanation: Sorted order makes the halving decision valid. The final single-element range must not be skipped.
